ARABIC LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #4
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ARABIC LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation.

2. When practising Imitative Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Imitative Speaking.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Imitative Speaking.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Imitative Speaking.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Imitative Speaking.

3. When practising Reading Aloud: Arabic Alphabet, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading Aloud: Arabic Alphabet.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading Aloud: Arabic Alphabet.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading Aloud: Arabic Alphabet.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading Aloud: Arabic Alphabet.

4. When practising Conversational Skills, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Conversational Skills.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Conversational Skills.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Conversational Skills.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Conversational Skills.

5. When practising Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening.

6. When practising Public Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Public Speaking.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Public Speaking.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Public Speaking.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Public Speaking.

7. In ARABIC LANGUAGE, the best classroom habit is: (1 mark)
   A. Only memorise without using the language
   B. Avoid speaking to classmates
   C. Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day
   D. Mix random languages with no purpose

8. When practising Phonological Awareness: Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Phonological Awareness: Fluency.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Phonological Awareness: Fluency.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological Awareness: Fluency.

9. When practising Interactive Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Interactive Speaking.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Interactive Speaking.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive Speaking.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
10. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Reading: Vocabulary Building and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

11. In three clear sentences, explain Guided writing: Arabic Alphabet and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

12. In three clear sentences, explain Guided writing: Handwriting and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing: Visuals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
